meta.title: Brand: Fizlet™ marks, lockups and colour · Fizlet
meta.description: The Fizlet™ and fzlt™ marks, lockups, ™ and casing rules, clear space, colour tokens and the Board UI kit, live, with every mark as an SVG download.

hero.lead: Fizlet™ is the micro animation and game engine for the DOM, by Chris Cooley ↗. Its short mark is fzlt™, also its npm scope. Every mark on this page is drawn live from the site's own tokens, and every one downloads as an SVG made from the same source.
hero.tm: Fizlet and fzlt are trademarks of Chris Cooley.

head.lead: Six letters and four, owned equally, each with the mark. FIZLET is the large logo: heavy caps, the mark's frame closed by the F. fzlt is the small logo: the mark's pixels and fzlt, always lowercase; the developer and npm mark, never a name in prose. Both in --ink, the pop in --k-attack on either ground.

sections.body:
• FIZLET logo

    The mark in its square frame; the frame's right side is the F's stem. Six heavy caps, drawn as outlines so they hold in any font. Titles, the hero, covers.

  • fzlt logo

    The mark's pixels without the frame, the pop above, then fzlt in bold lowercase. npm, code, badges, stickers and tight spaces.

The mark and the header lockup

The mark: pixel squares fizzing up a square frame, one popping. Frame and squares in --ink, the pop in --k-attack, on no tile: the logos' mark, 40px in the header, 34px at 380px and under. The version is a sticker, the site's sticker recipe in --k-sys. The header, the footer and fzlt.dev draw this one lockup. The favicon is the same mark: icon.svg.

DOM ENGINEV0.27.0FIZLET
DOM ENGINEV0.27.0FIZLET

Why fzlt. We picked fzlt on purpose, as Fizlet's developer and npm mark, so nobody mixes it up with anything else. It reads well as npm i fzlt. It has no vowels, so it is not a real word and not a misspelling of one. It has a “z”, one of the least-used letters in English. It won't autocorrect into anything, and nobody types it by accident. It is unique by design and it matches the brand: the @fzlt npm scope, github.com/fizlet ↗, Fizlet™ / fzlt™, and fzlt.dev and fzlt.app (planned redirects to fizlet.com). Today the install line is npm i @fzlt/core; plain fzlt is requested from npm, not ours yet, and the alias npm i fzlt@npm:@fzlt/core works now.

Fizlet

The brand: the name people remember. Confident, plain, arcade swagger. Headlines, pages, posts, the README title. It says the why, the mechanism, the proof.

  • README TITLE

    Fizlet™

  • HEADLINE

    Tiny physics for your page.

  • HEADLINE

    Recall gives the page back.

  • STICKER
    RECALLRESTORED

fzlt

The developer and npm mark. Short, dev-first, lowercase, code-shaped. npm, badges, CLI output, code comments, stickers. It says the what: the command, the brick, the number.

  • NPM DESCRIPTION
    fzlt™: Fizlet's micro animation and game engine for the DOM, by Chris Cooley. One loop, bounded everything, the page always comes back.
  • README BADGE LINE
    npm i @fzlt/core · kernel 3,372 B gzip · 0 runtime deps · MIT
  • SNIPPET COMMENT
    // fzlt/fx: sparks from the event ring. destroy() gives the page back.
  • STICKERS
    fzltRESTORED
    @fzlt/coreREADY

fzlt stays lowercase, even on a sticker; keep it out of kit labels that force capitals. The kernel size is measured on this build.

head.lead: The header lockup above, and three more. Only these; ™ never goes on code or a domain.

sections.body:
• Fizlet + fzlt

    Fizlet™ · fzlt™: the name, a middle dot, the short mark in mono and --muted.

  • @fzlt/core

    The package, in code style only, never with ™. Fizlet on npm is @fzlt/core: npm i @fzlt/core, bricks at @fzlt/core/<brick>.

  • fzlt.dev

    fizlet.com is the home. fzlt.dev (and fizlet.dev, fzlt.app) are planned redirects to it: lowercase, no ™, no link until live.

• Fizlet™ and fzlt™ carry ™ on the first prominent use on a surface: the hero, the footer, the README title, the npm description. Plain after that.
  • No ®. Nothing is registered.
  • The note: “Fizlet and fzlt are trademarks of Chris Cooley.”
  • Fizlet in prose and titles.
  • FIZLET as the wordmark only.
  • fizlet in URLs and code: fizlet.com.
  • fzlt always lowercase: the short mark and @fzlt/core.
  • Never FizLet.

• Logos: FIZLET at a 24px cap height, fzlt at 24px tall: the pop's smallest pixel stays about 1px.

  • FIZLET

    Header wordmark: 16px, the smallest it ships (the header at 380px wide and under).

  • Mark: 34px in page chrome; the favicon at the browser's size.

  • fzlt

    fzlt: 12px, the arcade key label size.

• FIZLET

    DON'T Stretched

    Never stretch, squash, slant or rotate a mark.

  • FIZLET

    DON'T Off-palette

    The tokens only: --ink, --muted, the tile's own colours.

  • FizLet

    DON'T FizLet

    Fizlet in prose, FIZLET as the mark. Never FizLet or FIZlet.

  • Fizlet®

    DON'T ®

    Nothing is registered. ™ only, never “registered”.

  • FZLT

    DON'T FZLT

    fzlt is always lowercase.

  • @fzlt™/core

    DON'T ™ in code

    No ™ in package names, imports or URLs.

sections.body:
The arcade key

One key family, one role each. Press one: the face drops onto its base. These only press.

Sticker keys

The big launch keys: a dark face, a white rim and base, a pixel icon tile.

Stickers

A kicker and one or two words, tilted −4°, on the rim: RECALL / RESTORED on the home demo, ERROR 404 / NO PAGE on the 404. Slam one: the kit's own drop, hit and press, then it settles.

@fzlt/core/arcade: the shell every page arcade game reuses, the overlay, scoreboard, keys and icons in this kit. It takes over the page, so it plays on its own pages, not this one.
